Glutathione: Frederick Hopkins. Glutathione (GSH,) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
Who is credited with discovering Blockchain?
Blockchain: Satoshi Nakamoto. A blockchain is a distributed ledger with growing lists of records (blocks) that are securely linked together via cryptographic hashes.
Who is credited with discovering Ethology?
Ethology: Isidore Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire. Ethology is a branch of zoology that studies the behaviour of non-human animals.

This British Formula One engineer, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest designers, has served as technical chief at Williams, McLaren, and Red Bull, and now co-owns Aston Martin's F1 team — who is he?
Adrian Newey (born 26 December 1958) is a British engineer, aerodynamicist, automotive designer, and motorsport executive.
Endemic to the rainforests of Sumatra, this plant grows an enormous inflorescence that blooms only rarely and briefly, emitting the stench of rotting flesh to lure pollinators — what plant is it?
Amorphophallus titanum is a flowering plant in the family Araceae.
Coined by a French naturalist in 1799 from a Tupi word for the sound macaws make, this genus name covers eight species of long-tailed, brightly plumed Neotropical parrots — which genus?
Ara (bird) is a Neotropical genus of macaws with eight extant species and at least two extinct species.
One of the first grains ever domesticated, this cereal crop was cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9000 BC and later spread throughout Eurasia by 2000 BC — name the grain?
Barley (Hordeum vulgare), a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.
So dense that not even light can escape its gravity, this astronomical object's boundary of no return is called the event horizon — name it?
Black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.
With a mass roughly 13 to 80 times Jupiter's, these substellar objects glow faintly from deuterium fusion rather than true hydrogen burning — what's the term for them?
Brown dwarf are substellar objects that have more mass than the biggest gas giant planets, but less than the least massive main-sequence stars.

Made of one oxygen atom triple-bonded to a single atom of the element that also forms diamonds and graphite, this colorless, odorless, poisonous gas is slightly less dense than air and typically arises from incomplete combustion — name the compound?
Carbon monoxide (chemical formula CO) is a poisonous, flammable gas that is colorless, odorless, tasteless, and slightly less dense than air.

Used to disinfect skin before surgery, sterilize surgical tools, treat oral yeast infections, and keep urinary catheters clear, this antiseptic compound comes as a gluconate or acetate salt — what is it?
Chlorhexidine is a disinfectant and antiseptic which is used for skin disinfection before surgery and to disinfect surgical instruments.
This bird group's rock-dove species gave rise to most domesticated pigeon breeds, including racing and fantail pigeons, and was later introduced to the Americas — which classification is it?
Columba (genus) comprises a genus of medium to large pigeons.
This bird family, the sole one in its taxonomic order, includes roadrunners, koels, malkohas, and coucals across roughly 150 species. Name the family?
Cuckoo are birds in the family Cuculidae, the sole taxon in the order Cuculiformes.

Occurring five times in the phrase 'no highway cowboys,' this linguistic term describes two vowel sounds gliding together within a single syllable, contrasting with a single steady vowel sound — what is it?
Diphthong (DIP-), also known as a gliding vowel or a vowel glide, is a combination of two adjacent vowel sounds within the same syllable.
Once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil, these true seals of the genus Mirounga are named for the male's large trunk-like snout, with males weighing up to 4,000 kilograms — which animal?
Elephant seal are very large, oceangoing true seals in the genus Mirounga.
Genus Vespa's largest eusocial wasp, this insect was introduced to North America as early as 1840 and remains the only true member of its genus found there — what is it?
European hornet (Vespa crabro) is the largest eusocial wasp native to Europe.
Holding doctorates in both medicine and philosophy from Pisa by age 21, this Italian naturalist became the "founder of experimental biology" by disproving spontaneous generation — who was he?
Francesco Redi (18 February 1626 - 1 March 1697) was an Italian physician, naturalist, biologist, and poet.
The most aggressive and common cancer to originate in the brain, this tumor is thought to arise from cells called astrocytes and carries a grim prognosis — what is it?
Glioblastoma (GBM), is the most aggressive and most common type of cancer that originates in the brain, and has a very poor prognosis for survival.
This Austrian physician wrote over 300 publications and termed his diagnosis of autism 'autistic psychopathy,' though later allegations tied him to a Nazi-era clinic in Vienna — what was his name?
Hans Asperger (18 February 1906 - 21 October 1980) was an Austrian physician.
Which cosmological relationship says a galaxy's recession speed is proportional to its distance from Earth, discovered via redshift measurements and usually credited to a 1929 paper?
Hubble's law is the observation in physical cosmology that galaxies are moving away from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance.
Usually caused by the Epstein–Barr virus and nicknamed 'glandular fever,' which illness brings fever, sore throat, swollen neck nodes, and a fatigue that can linger for months?
Infectious mononucleosis (IM, mono), also known as glandular fever, is an infection usually caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).

Called 'the greatest investor on Wall Street,' this founder of Renaissance Technologies made his fortune using mathematical models, after co-developing a key concept in differential geometry — who is he?
Jim Simons (April 25, 1938 - May 10, 2024) was an American hedge fund manager, investor, mathematician, and philanthropist.
Which German engineer and economist founded the World Economic Forum in 1971 and chaired it until stepping down in 2025?
Klaus Schwab (born 30 March 1938) is a German mechanical engineer, economist, and founder of the World Economic Forum (WEF).
This big-cat hybrid, born of a male lion and a female tiger, is the largest of all living cats, growing larger than either parent and enjoying a swim. What animal is it?
Liger is a hybrid offspring of a male lion (Panthera leo) and a tigress, or female tiger (Panthera tigris).

Developed by MathWorks, this proprietary programming language and numeric computing environment is built around matrix manipulation, and pairs with an add-on called Simulink for graphical simulation and model-based design. What software is this?
MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
It's the science and practice of diagnosing, treating, and preventing disease — from pharmaceuticals and surgery to splints, psychotherapy, and ionizing radiation. What is this field?
Medicine is the science and practice of caring for patients, managing the diagnosis, prognosis, prevention, treatment and palliation of their injury or disease, while promoting their health.
Some of these tiny eight-legged arachnids live in soil as decomposers, others on plants causing galls, and one destructive parasite targets honeybee colonies — what are they?
Mite are small arachnids (eight-legged arthropods) of two large orders, the Acariformes and the Parasitiformes, which were historically grouped together in the subclass Acari.
This genus of spring-blooming perennials in the amaryllis family is better known by common names like daffodil and jonquil, with trumpet-shaped flowers usually white and yellow. What is it?
Narcissus (plant) is a genus of predominantly spring flowering perennial plants of the amaryllis family, Amaryllidaceae.
This family of three long, ribbon-like pelagic fish species includes the longest bony fish alive, stretching up to about 8 meters, yet rarely seen by humans — what fish is it?
Oarfish are the three species of large and extremely long pelagic lampriform fish belonging to the small family Regalecidae.

This genus of 70 to 100 frost-tolerant annual, biennial, and perennial species native to temperate Eurasia, Africa, and North America is the type genus of its flowering plant family — what's the genus?
Papaver is a genus of 70-100 species of frost-tolerant annuals, biennials, and perennials native to temperate and cold regions of Eurasia, Africa and North America.

This cellular process, in which a cell's outer membrane engulfs a large particle to form an internal compartment, is a key immune-system mechanism for clearing pathogens and cellular debris — what is it called?

Phagocytosis (from Ancient Greek (phagein) 'to eat' and (kytos) 'cell') is the process by which a cell uses its plasma membrane to engulf a large particle (0.5 m), giving rise to an internal compartment called the phagosome.
This radioactive, silvery-gray actinide metal with atomic number 94 forms oxides in moist air that can expand a sample by up to 70% in volume — which element?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
This thorny European shrub's tart fruit flavors a British gin, while its tough wood traditionally makes an Irish walking stick — what plant is it (scientific name)?
Prunus spinosa is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
First flown in 1955 as a nuclear-strike follow-on to the Mach 1 Super Sabre, this fighter-bomber earned the nickname 'Thud' and flew most early Vietnam War strike missions — which aircraft?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief is an American fighter-bomber that served with the United States Air Force from 1958 to 1984.
One of the world's oldest crops, this thistle-like annual plant with globular orange or red flower heads is grown commercially today for oil pressed from its seeds — what is it?
Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
Domesticated well over 3,000 years ago and grown widely in India, Myanmar, and Sudan today, this plant is considered one of the oldest oilseed crops known to humanity — what is it?
Sesame (Sesamum indicum) is a plant in the genus Sesamum, also called benne.
The largest of the toothed whales and the largest toothed predator alive, this pelagic giant has females who give birth only every four to twenty years — what is it?
Sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) is the largest of the toothed whales and the largest toothed predator.

Which British single-seat fighter plane, the only such aircraft Britain produced continuously throughout World War II, was famous for its innovative elliptical wing designed to be as thin as possible?
Supermarine Spitfire is a British single-seat fighter aircraft that was used by the Royal Air Force and other Allied countries before, during, and after World War II.
Raised by a wealthy uncle after his father fled following a fight, this English philosopher laid out an influential social contract theory in his 1651 book 'Leviathan' — who is he?

Thomas Hobbes (HOBZ; 5 April 1588 - 4 December 1679) was an English philosopher and political theorist, best known for his 1651 book Leviathan, in which he expounds an influential formulation of social contract theory.

These simple-looking marine invertebrates prove their kinship to vertebrates as larvae, when they sport a notochord, a dorsal nerve cord, and a post-anal tail — resembling a tiny tadpole. What are they?
Tunicate are marine invertebrates belonging to the subphylum Tunicata.
This canid genus contains the 'true foxes' — smaller and bushier-tailed than any wolf or jackal, typically living two to four years, occasionally a decade — which genus?
Vulpes is a genus of the subfamily Caninae.
Also known as AZT, this was the very first antiretroviral drug used against HIV/AIDS, and can be given during birth to prevent mother-to-child spread — what is it?
Zidovudine (ZDV), also known as azidothymidine (AZT), was the first antiretroviral medication used to prevent and treat HIV/AIDS.
This nucleoside, a building block of RNA, gives rise to the energy carriers ATP and ADP and is used as an intravenous drug for certain irregular heartbeats — what is it?
Working at a Soviet computing centre in 1985, this engineer designed one of history's most famous puzzle games — yet saw no royalties from it until founding a company around it in 1996. Who is he?
Domesticated in Southwest China roughly 2,000 years ago, this corm-producing plant is nicknamed 'devil's tongue' and gets boiled down into a jelly-like noodle called shirataki — what is it?
Amorphophallus konjac: Edible plant from Yunnan, China.
NATO codenamed 'Cub,' this four-engine Soviet turboprop served for three decades as the standard cargo and paratroop transport of the Soviet Air Forces — which aircraft?
Antonov An-12: Soviet medium-range transport aircraft.
Caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides and spread through food tainted with eggs, this infection most often hits children and is symptomless in over 85% of cases — what is it?
Ascariasis: Disease caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides. The eggs hatch in the intestines, the larvae burrow through the gut wall, and migrate to the lungs via the blood.

Among the first life forms on Earth and typically just a few micrometres long, these single-celled prokaryotes thrive everywhere from hot springs to radioactive waste and drive the putrefaction stage of decay — what are they?
Native to Southeast Asia, the heart-shaped leaves of this pepper-family vine are chewed with areca nut, despite links to serious health risks — which plant?
Betel: Species of plant. Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.
Launched as the 7X7 program in 1978 and designed to complement the larger 747, which American wide-body airliner first entered service with United Airlines in 1982?
This Asian insect species, first found in Pennsylvania in 1998, cost Mid-Atlantic apple growers $37 million in a single year and now threatens hazelnut harvests worldwide — what is it?

Brown marmorated stink bug: Species of Pentatomid insect. The brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.
Cultivated since China's Song Dynasty and boasting thousands of ornamental cultivars, which flowering shrub from the tea family is native to forests of China and Japan?
Camellia japonica: Species of flowering plant.
A woody shrub native to South America, this starchy tuber yields tapioca and, when grated and toasted, becomes Brazil's farofa and West Africa's garri — what crop is it?
Cassava: Staple crop. Although a perennial plant, cassava is extensively cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions as an annual crop for its edible starchy tuberous root.
Released by OpenAI in November 2022 and built on generative pre-trained transformers, this chatbot is widely credited with setting off the current AI boom. Name it.

ChatGPT is a generative AI chatbot developed by OpenAI, originally released in November 2022, using large language models — specifically generative pre-trained transformers — and it accelerated the ongoing AI boom.

An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned his observations into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen food industry — and a famous brand bears his name. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye: American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist.

A summer migrant to Europe and Asia that winters in Africa, this bird tricks other species into raising its young by laying eggs that mimic the host's, and even disguises itself as a hawk — what bird is it?
Common cuckoo: Species of bird. It is a brood parasite, which means it lays eggs in the nests of other bird species, particularly of dunnocks, meadow pipits, and reed warblers.
Nicknamed the mosquito hawk, which long-legged insect of the superfamily Tipuloidea is often mistaken for an oversized mosquito?
Crane fly: Superfamily of flies. The larvae of crane flies are known commonly as leatherjackets.
This World Wide Web content sits on overlay networks that use the Internet but cannot be reached with an ordinary browser. What does reaching it require?
The dark web is World Wide Web content that exists on darknets — overlay networks that use the Internet but require specific software, configurations or authorization to access.
Produced by the enzyme 5α-reductase acting on a more familiar male sex hormone, this compound is a more potent driver of prostate growth, sebum, and body hair — which hormone?
Sometimes called 'word blindness,' this learning disability makes it hard to spell, sound out words, and read quickly, and often co-occurs with ADHD — what is it?
The tallest and heaviest of all living penguins, this flightless Antarctic bird can top 45 kilograms and sports bright-yellow ear patches — which species is it?
Emperor penguin: Large flightless seabird endemic to Antarctica.
This Marine-turned-professor's 1981 memoir about fighting at Peleliu and Okinawa later inspired Ken Burns's The War and HBO's The Pacific, where he was played by Joseph Mazzello — who is he?
Made up mostly of undigested food broken down by gut bacteria, this bodily waste is expelled through the anus and can even be dried for fuel or used as fertilizer — what is it?
Feces: Solid or semisolid remains of undigested food.

First described by 19th-century French psychiatrists Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, this rare condition — also called shared psychotic disorder — lets one person's delusion spread to another. What is it called?

Folie à deux: Shared psychosis, a psychotic disorder. The disorder, first conceptualized in 19th century French psychiatry by Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, is also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome.

Named after Scottish naturalist Alexander Garden and first proposed in 1753 by botanist Jane Colden, this fragrant flowering genus in the coffee family is native to Africa, Asia and Australia — which plant genus?
Gardenia: Genus of flowering plants in the coffee family Rubiaceae.
Nicknamed the blue dragon, this pelagic sea slug floats upside down using surface tension and a stomach gas bubble, and feeds on the Portuguese man o' war — what is it?
With long, whip-like antennae and a global range except Antarctica, this insect family — known as true crickets — includes burrowing giants that dig meter-deep tunnels. What is the family called?
Gryllidae: Family of crickets. The family Gryllidae contains the subfamilies and genera which entomologists now term true crickets.
This German physicist was the first to conclusively demonstrate the electromagnetic waves predicted by James Clerk Maxwell's equations — who is he?
This genus of great apes emerged from Australopithecus and includes modern humans alongside extinct relatives, with chimpanzees and bonobos as its closest living kin — what genus is it?
Homo: Genus of hominins. Homo erectus and Homo neanderthalensis) classified as either ancestral or closely related to modern humans, collectively called archaic humans.

When the thyroid gland churns out too much hormone, the result can be a racing heartbeat, heat intolerance, hand tremor and weight loss — and rarely, a life-threatening 'thyroid storm.' What is this condition?
Hyperthyroidism: Excessive production of thyroid hormone.
Covering patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets, this legal category of intangible creations first developed as a concept in 17th- and 18th-century England — what is it called?
Intellectual property: Ownership of creative expressions and processes.
Known as sampaguita in the Philippines, where it's the national flower, this fragrant vine or shrub also lends its blossoms to a beloved variety of tea — which species?
Jasminum sambac: Species of jasmine. Jasminum sambac (Arabian jasmine or Sambac jasmine or Mogra) is a species of jasmine native to Bhutan and India.
Also nicknamed the reed or swamp feline, this solitary wild predator ranges from the Caucasus to Southeast Asia and marks territory by urine spraying — which species?
Biosynthesized in the body from the amino acid tyrosine, this compound is the direct precursor to dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine — what is it?
L-DOPA: Chemical compound. As is true for many molecules, the human body produces only one of these isomers (the l-DOPA form).

Elon Musk's praise for his MIT driver-attention study on Tesla's autopilot brought this computer scientist to prominence in 2019, ahead of a career hosting long-form interviews with notable figures — who is he?
Lex Fridman: American scientist and podcast host (born 1983)
Sold as Ativan, this benzodiazepine treats anxiety, insomnia, and active seizures, and is even used during surgery to interfere with memory formation — what medication is it?
Lorazepam: Benzodiazepine medication. Lorazepam, sold under the brand name Ativan among others, is a benzodiazepine medication.
Produced when beta-amylase breaks starch down two glucose units at a time, which reducing disaccharide gets its name from the germinating-seed process of malting?
Grown from the YF-17 that lost the Air Force's lightweight fighter contest, which twin-engine carrier jet won a second life when the Navy picked it instead?
McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet: American carrier-capable multirole strike aircraft.
A physician-turned-hedge-fund-manager, this investor famously predicted the subprime mortgage crisis and was portrayed in the 2015 film The Big Short — who is he?
Michael Burry: American hedge fund manager (born 1971)
Nicknamed 'water warts,' this viral skin infection causes small pink bumps with a telltale dimple in the center and usually clears up on its own within a year — what is it?

Molluscum contagiosum: Viral infection of the skin. Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.
This lipid-rich substance wraps around nerve axons in segments, leaving gaps called nodes of Ranvier that let electrical signals leap along in a process called saltatory conduction — what is it?
Myelin: Fatty substance insulating nerve cell axons.
This British-American historian, a senior fellow at Stanford's Hoover Institution, writes on financial history and holds notably favorable views of the British Empire — who is he?
Known as holy basil and sacred within the Vaishnava tradition of Hinduism, which aromatic herb is widely used in Ayurvedic tea?
Ocimum tenuiflorum: Species of flowering plant.
Also called a steer or bullock, and usually yoked in pairs, which castrated male bovine has long served as a draft animal for ploughing and hauling?
Ox: Common bovine draft and riding animal.
Nicknamed the empress tree for its fast growth and showy foxglove-like blooms, which East Asian hardwood has become an invasive species across the Eastern US?
Paulownia tomentosa: Species of deciduous tree classified in its own family.
Its name combines the Greek words for 'love' and 'tree,' and with over 600 accepted species it's the second-largest genus in the arum family after Anthurium — which popular houseplant genus?
Caused by viral infections, autoimmune disorders, or pulmonary embolism, this condition inflames the membranes lining the lungs and chest cavity, causing sharp pain when breathing — which condition?
Pleurisy: Disease of the lungs. Pleurisy, also known as pleuritis, is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
Caused by a single mutation in the LMNA gene, this rare disorder causes children to age dramatically faster than normal, with most not living past their twenties — which condition?
Progeria: Genetic disorder that causes early aging.
In Euclidean geometry, which fundamental relation says the square on a right triangle's longest side equals the sum of the squares on the other two — famously written a² + b² = c²?
Pythagorean theorem: Relation between sides of a right triangle.
This biological process comes in two forms — asexual, as seen in cloning, and sexual, which combines gametes carrying half the usual chromosome count — what's the process called?
Reproduction: Biological process. Reproduction (or procreation or breeding) is the biological process by which new individual organisms – offspring – are produced from their parent or parents.
The second woman ever to win the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine — and the first American-born one — this physicist shared the 1977 award for developing the radioimmunoassay. Who was she?
Rosalyn Sussman Yalow: American medical physicist (1921–2011)

First used in English in the early 15th century and possibly named after a Mediterranean island, this term covers small oily forage fish under 15 centimeters, with larger ones called pilchards — what's the fish?
Sardine: Common name for various small, oily forage fish.
Sold as Zoloft, this SSRI antidepressant treats major depression, OCD, panic disorder, and social anxiety, with common side effects like nausea and insomnia — what is it?
Sertraline: SSRI antidepressant. It should not be used together with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs): this combination may cause serotonin syndrome, which can be life-threatening in some cases.
Known by the E number E211, this white crystalline salt of benzoic acid is a widely used food preservative and pickling agent — what is it?
Sodium benzoate: Common food preservative. It appears as a white crystalline chemical with the formula C6H5COONa.
Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes,' this genus of spherical, grape-clustered bacteria can grow with or without oxygen — which genus?
Comprising around 90 species split between river martins and all other members, this family of aerial-feeding songbirds is thought to have evolved as hole-nesters in Africa — what are they called?
Swallow: Family of songbirds. The term "swallow" is used as the common name for Hirundo rustica in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

Found at the ends of linear chromosomes, this repetitive DNA region works with specialized proteins to prevent the chromosome tip from being mistaken for a damaging double-strand break — what is it called?
Telomere: Region of repetitive nucleotide sequences on chromosomes.
The largest cat of the genus Panthera, this Asian apex predator wears orange fur with mostly vertical black stripes and ranges from snowy Russian forests to tropical Indian jungles — what is it?
Closely related to salmon, these carnivorous freshwater fish spawn in shallow gravel beds of headwater creeks after migrating upstream — what are they called?
Trout: Freshwater fish from subfamily Salmoninae.
Used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder, this medication carries a serious risk of birth defects if taken during pregnancy — what is it?
Valproate: Medication used for epilepsy, bipolar disorder and migraine. Common side effects of valproate include nausea, vomiting, somnolence, and dry mouth.
Also known as ash pumpkin or winter melon, this South and Southeast Asian plant is grown for its very large fruit, eaten as a vegetable once mature — which plant?
Wax gourd: Species of vine and edible fruit.
This Japanese media artist and academic directs a research centre for 'Digital Nature' and holds visiting professorships at multiple Japanese art universities — who is he?
Yoichi Ochiai: Japanese academic, artist, and entrepreneur. Yoichi Ochiai (落合 陽一, Yoichi Ochiai; born 16 September 1987) is a Japanese media artist, entrepreneur, and academic.
What is the chemical symbol for tin?
The symbol for tin is Sn. Tin is a chemical element; it has the symbol Sn and atomic number 50.
What is the chemical symbol for copernicium?
The symbol for copernicium is Cn. Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.

O. J. Simpson: Orenthal James Simpson (July 9, 1947 – April 10, 2024), nicknamed "the Juice", was an American football player, actor, and media personality.

James Dean: James Byron Dean (February 8, 1931 – September 30, 1955) was an American actor.

Ronald Reagan: Ronald Wilson Reagan (February 6, 1911 – June 5, 2004) was an American politician and actor who served as the 40th president of the United States from 1981 to 1989.
